2027-02-20.title: Saturday of the First Week of Lent
readings: You shall be a people holy to the Lord your God
Blessed are they who follow the law of the Lord!
Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect
2027-02-20.alt: Lenten weekday, First Week of Lent. The Alleluia is omitted throughout Lent; the Gloria is omitted except on solemnities and feasts. Liturgical colour: violet.
2027-02-20.verse: But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,
theo: Moses, at the end of his long journey with Israel, describes the covenant as a solemn exchange of promises made “this very day”. “Today you have obtained the LORD's agreement: to be your God; and for you to walk in his ways… Today the LORD has obtained your agreement: to be his treasured people.” It sounds almost like a marriage vow. God binds himself to Israel, and Israel binds itself to God. The word “treasured” translates the Hebrew segullah, the private treasure a king keeps for himself apart from the state treasury. Israel is God's personal treasure, set “high above all nations”, not for pride but to be “a people holy to the LORD your God”. Every Christian has made this same exchange of promises at baptism, and every Mass renews it. In Lent we are invited to say again, “today”, that we belong to him and will walk in his ways.

Jesus now shows how far the ways of God reach. “You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’ But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be children of your Father in heaven; for he makes his sun rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the righteous and on the unrighteous.” The sun does not choose whom to warm. If we love only those who love us, Jesus says, we are doing nothing more than tax collectors and pagans. Then comes the summit of the Sermon: “Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.” This perfection is not flawlessness but completeness of love: a love that, like the Father's, excludes no one. It is impossible on our own; it is the work of grace in God's treasured people. As the first week of Lent ends, we bring to God the one person we find hardest to love, and we pray for them by name.
outline: Ask: whom do you find hardest to pray for?
Like the sun on the evil and the good.
“Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.”
live: Pray today for someone who has wronged you, by name, asking God to bless them.
Greet warmly someone you usually ignore.
2027-02-20.prayer: Father in heaven, you make your sun rise on the evil and on the good, and you have chosen us as your treasured people. Renew in us today the promises of our baptism. Give us a heart like yours, that we may love our enemies, pray for those who persecute us, and grow towards the perfection of your love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: Every Mass renews the covenant: in the Blood of the new and eternal covenant, God says again “you are mine”, and we answer “Amen”. Christ, who prayed for his persecutors from the cross, teaches us to pray for ours.

quick: God and Israel make a covenant: you are my treasured people.
Jesus says: love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.
Be perfect in love, as the Father is perfect.
2027-02-20.action: Pray by name for someone who has hurt you.
2027-02-20.question: Whom have I excluded from my love, and what would it take to include them?

family.explain: Jesus says: love even the people who are unkind to you, and pray for them. God makes the sun shine on everyone, good and bad. We are his children, so we must love like him.
family.intention: We pray for people who are unkind to us.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone who is unkind to us whom we can pray for tonight?”

illus: In 1999 Graham Staines, an Australian missionary who had cared for leprosy patients in Odisha for decades, was burned to death with his two young sons by a mob. A few days later his widow, Gladys, told the press that she had forgiven the killers and had no bitterness. She stayed on in India for years to continue the work among leprosy patients. Many in India who had never read the Gospel said they understood what Jesus meant by loving enemies when they heard her words.

pm.open: Father, you are kind to the good and the evil. Make us your children, perfect in love. Amen.
share: Today the LORD has obtained your agreement: to be his treasured people (Deuteronomy 26:18). Do I know that I am God's treasure?
Love your enemies (Matthew 5:44). Who is my enemy?
Be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect (Matthew 5:48). Where does my love stop short?
pm.resp: Happy are those who walk in the law of the LORD.
interc: For those who persecute Christians, that they may meet Christ.
For victims of violence, that they may find healing and the grace to forgive.
For nations and communities divided by hatred.
For catechumens preparing for baptism at Easter.
For our group, that we may love without exception.
pm.close: Father, your Son prayed for those who crucified him. Give us his heart, that we may love as you love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Moses tells Israel: today you have obtained the LORD's agreement: to be your God… Today the LORD has obtained your agreement: to be his treasured people (Deuteronomy 26:17–18). It is like a marriage vow between God and his people.
At baptism we made the same covenant. We are God's treasured people. Lent is the time to say again, today: I am yours, and I will walk in your ways.

Jesus shows us how far God's ways reach: love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be children of your Father in heaven; for he makes his sun rise on the evil and on the good (Matthew 5:44–45).

Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect (Matthew 5:48). Not flawless, but complete in love. As this first week of Lent ends, let us pray by name for the one person we find hardest to love. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says: love even people who are unkind to you, and pray for them. The sun shines on everyone! Tonight, pray for someone who was not nice to you.

intro: Theme: “Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.”
God's treasured people, a love as wide as the sunrise, and the perfection of the Father.

q: Today the LORD has obtained your agreement: to be his treasured people, as he promised you, and to keep his commandments;
But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's own people, in order that you may proclaim the mighty acts of him who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises in prayer tonight.

sub: Not only those who love us.
q: If your enemies are hungry, give them bread to eat; and if they are thirsty, give them water to drink;
But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,
points.apply: Do one kind act for someone who has opposed you.

q: Happy are those whose way is blameless, who walk in the law of the LORD.
Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.
points.apply: Ask God each morning of Lent to widen your love by one person.

concl: We are God's treasured people by covenant.
Our love becomes perfect when, like the Father's, it excludes no one.
2027-02-20.resolve: Pray every day of Lent for one person who has hurt you.
